text:
Maya R.: Heads-up: starting May 1 we’re launching a pilot we’re calling 'Flex Float' — you can convert up to 2 unused PTO days into floating holidays (max 3 floating days total/year) for things like cultural observances, caregiving, or short travel. Details + FAQ: https://intranet.redwood.com/policies/flex-float

Samir P.: Quick q — does converting days change accruals or payroll?

Maya R.: No, accrual rates remain the same. This is a balance conversion only (we move days from your available PTO bucket into a floating-holiday bucket). Payroll unaffected.

Lina G.: How do we request the conversion? self-serve in Workday or need manager sign-off?

Maya R.: Good Q — conversion is self-serve but requires one-click manager acknowledgement. Flow: Workday > Time Off > Convert PTO to Floating Holiday > pick up to 2 days > submit > manager acknowledges. We’ll add an automated reminder to managers.

Anya C.: Is this pro-rated for new hires and global offices?

Maya R.: Pro-rated for hires within first 90 days. For international offices we’ll honor local law — some countries can’t do conversion; policy page lists country exceptions.

Lina G.: Are floating holidays eligible for rollover?

Maya R.: Floating holidays expire at year-end and cannot be cashed out. You can convert PTO into floating holidays through Nov 1 each year; any unused floating days expire Dec 31.

Samir P.: For coverage planning — is there a recommended notice window to take a float?

Maya R.: We ask teams to follow standard PTO notice guidelines (2 business days for 1-day requests, more for longer leaves). Managers can approve/deny based on coverage. If a team has a critical release, we ask flexibility, but we’ll surface conflicts in the manager dashboard.

People Ops Bot: :information_source: New policy posted: "Flex Float pilot — May 1 to Oct 31". See: https://intranet.redwood.com/policies/flex-float. HRIS task created for all managers.

Samir P.: One more travel-related note: any changes to travel preclearance or code-of-conduct for company-sponsored travel?

Maya R.: Yes — we updated the Travel Code section. Highlights: everyone traveling on company funds must complete the Travel Conduct Acknowledgement in Concur 72 hours before departure, and review the Travel Safety Checklist. If you’ll be abroad >14 days we require a pre-trip security check-in with People Ops. Link: https://intranet.redwood.com/policies/travel-conduct

Lina G.: What if someone misses the 72-hour ack?

Maya R.: Concur will block travel bookings after 72 hours without acknowledgement; managers can override for urgent cases, but it generates an audit flag.

Anya C.: Are there K-18 / vaccination rules being added?

Maya R.: We’re not requiring medical documentation broadly, but certain regions (listed on the policy page) have entry requirements. For those trips People Ops will reach out with guidance.

Samir P.: Appreciate the clarity. Will you send a short blurb team leads can forward?

Maya R.: Yes — I’ll drop a TL;DR kit in #managers in 15. It will include 2 ready-to-send lines, a sample Concur message, and the Workday steps.

Lina G.: Thanks — could we get a reminder when the pilot ends? want to track team utilization.

Maya R.: We’ll run utilization reports and share a dashboard mid-pilot (Aug) and final report after Oct 31.

Samir P.: :thumbsup:

Maya R.: If you have edge cases, DM me or email people-ops@redwood.com. Thanks everyone!
